Introduction and meaning
Public nuisance. BNS restatement of IPC 268. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 268. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 270 is the rule on “Public nuisance”. The section provides that . A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity, or which must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, danger or annoyance to persons who may have occasion to use any public right but a common nuisance is not excused on the ground that it causes some convenience or advantage. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 270 exists so that “Public nuisance” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.

examples.body: A short everyday fact pattern is tested against “Public nuisance”. Name BNS s. 270, list the ingredients, and say which facts match. This is a teaching example — the statute does not print a numbered illustration under this heading.

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 270 (Public nuisance) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 270 (Public nuisance), Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) . A person is guilty of a public nuisance who does any act or is guilty of an illegal omission which causes any common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or to the people in general who dwell or occupy property in the vicinity, or which must necessarily cause injury, obstruction, danger or annoyance to persons who may have occasion to use any public right but a common nuisance is not excused on the ground that it causes some convenience or advantage
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 270 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 270 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

misconceptions.trap: Writing only the section number and title without analyzing ingredients or case ratio.
misconceptions.correction: An authoritative note defines the concept, lists ingredients, uses an illustration, states explanations/exceptions, applies the test, and concludes with BNS s. 270.

misconceptions.trap: Copying a statutory illustration without mapping it to an ingredient.
misconceptions.correction: Quote the illustration, then write which ingredient it proves or which ingredient is missing. Mapping is the core evidentiary link.

misconceptions.trap: Giving a one-line summary or shortened explanation of the provision.
misconceptions.correction: Authoritative chamber practice and judicial papers require a complete answer. The analysis on this page is written at full length for that reason.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Analytical comment. Explain a condition, a proviso, or a practical difficulty in applying s. 270. Do not invent case names.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 270.”
